title: Units and Measurements
subject: Physics
summary: Units and Measurements is the foundation chapter of Class 11 Physics. It introduces physical quantities, SI units, dimensions, significant figures, measurement errors, Vernier Calipers, Screw Gauge, and dimensional analysis. A strong understanding of this chapter helps in solving numerical problems accurately throughout Physics and is frequently tested in JEE Main and Advanced.
formulas: Mean Absolute Error = (ΔA₁ + ΔA₂ + ... + ΔAₙ) / n
Percentage Error in Multiplication/Division = Percentage Error of A + Percentage Error of B
Least Count of Vernier Calipers = 1 MSD − 1 VSD
Least Count of Screw Gauge = Pitch / Number of Circular Scale Divisions
keyPoints: Every physical quantity is expressed as a numerical value along with its unit.
The International System of Units (SI) consists of seven fundamental units from which all derived units are obtained.
Dimensions represent the powers of fundamental quantities such as Mass, Length, and Time.
Dimensional analysis is useful for checking the correctness of physical equations and deriving relationships between quantities.
Significant figures indicate the precision of a measured value and should always be maintained during calculations.
Absolute, relative, and percentage errors are important for estimating the accuracy of experimental measurements.
Random errors can be reduced by taking multiple observations, while systematic errors arise due to faulty instruments or incorrect methods.
Vernier Calipers and Screw Gauge are precision measuring instruments commonly used to measure small lengths and diameters.
Always apply zero-error correction before calculating the final reading from measuring instruments.
Correct unit conversion and proper rounding rules are essential for obtaining accurate numerical answers.
pyqs: JEE Main: Questions based on dimensional analysis, SI units, and significant figures are frequently asked.
JEE Main: Numerical problems involving Vernier Calipers, Screw Gauge, and error calculations appear regularly.
JEE Advanced: Multi-concept problems combining dimensions, error propagation, and precision instruments are common.
JEE Advanced: Dimensional consistency and derivation of relations using dimensional analysis are high-weightage topics.

practiceQuestions.q: If Energy, Velocity, and Time are chosen as the fundamental quantities, determine the dimensions of Surface Tension.
The least count of a Vernier Calipers is 0.01 cm and its zero error is +0.03 cm. If the observed reading is 5.26 cm, calculate the corrected length.
A measurement has an absolute error of 0.2 cm and the measured value is 20 cm. Find the percentage error.
